title: Felix and the Thorn
premise: Xanthe Reyes was sold to the crown as a child and raised in the poison-proofed valley of Vell, where wards keep out magic and tasters like him are kept alive only as long as they're useful. When the valley's wards collapse on the night every star vanishes from the sky, Xanthe learns the truth: the court beneath the mountain has called in an old debt—the soul of his dead mother, bargained away before he was born—and the king intends to pay it with Xanthe instead. Fleeing with a disgraced hedge-witch named Odile and a runaway kitchen boy who can hear the mountain speaking, Xanthe must reach the Undercourt before midwinter and win back not just his mother's soul but his own. He succeeds by refusing to bargain at all: he shames the mountain's dying queen into honoring a debt she never wanted to collect, and returns to a kingdom learning that justice sometimes lives outside its laws.
about_author: Felix Yarrow spent seven years as a line cook in a mountain resort town before turning to fantasy, and he still measures every fictional feast by whether he could actually make it. Felix and the Thorn is their first novel, written mostly during night shifts and finished in a rented cabin where, reassuringly, no stars went out.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A routine day in the royal kitchens of Vell: tasting the king's supper, cataloguing flavors, dodging the steward's cruelty. We learn the valley's rules—no magic crosses the wards, and tasters never leave. Xanthe tastes something wrong in a honey cake and quietly pockets it. Beat: quiet competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Honey Held
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The honey cake contains powdered thornroot—a poison that shouldn't exist inside the wards. Investigating, Xanthe finds Odile, a hedge-witch imprisoned in the cellar for smuggling remedies to servants. She recognizes the thornroot as Undercourt work. Beat: first crack in Xanthe's safe little world; wary alliance begins.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At midnight every star goes dark, and the valley's wards fall with them like cut strings. Cold pours in; the kitchens panic. In the chaos, Odile escapes her cell, and the mountain to the north glows faintly green. Beat: awe and terror—the world is bigger and more dangerous than promised.

chapters.title: A Debt Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The king summons Xanthe privately and reveals the truth: his mother sold her unborn son's soul to the Undercourt for one year of life, and now that the wards are down, the debt comes due at midwinter. The king plans to deliver him. Beat: betrayal—the family he never knew left him a death sentence.

chapters.title: Running the Valley Line
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, opening with flight. Xanthe steals out through the wine cellars with Odile, who knows the old ward-roads. They pick up Tam, a kitchen boy who claims the mountain has been whispering his name since the stars died. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; found family takes its first shape.

chapters.title: The Thorn Road
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. On the road north through frost-killed farmland, Odile explains the Undercourt: a court of the dead beneath the mountain, ruled by a queen who collects debts no living law will honor. Villagers burn charms against them. Tam hears the whispers growing louder. Beat: dread building; the cost of the journey becomes real.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse at Grayford
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The trio shelters in a tollhouse where a toll-collector demands payment in memories. Xanthe offers a memory of his mother's face—and realizes he's already lost it, traded away piece by piece by the debt itself. Odile cheats the toll with sleight-of-hand. Beat: grief without a face to grieve; Odile's loyalty deepens.

chapters.title: Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The city of Hollow Bells, where the king's riders hunt runaways. The trio hides among a festival of masked mourners. Xanthe is nearly recognized by the king's spymaster, a man who once fed him dinner like a father. Beat: the past as a trap; Xanthe chooses the strangers over the kingdom that raised him.

chapters.title: The Spymaster's Mercy
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Cornered on a bridge, Xanthe expects arrest—but the spymaster lets him go, revealing the king means to bind Xanthe's soul to the throne's protection forever, worse than any debt. 'Run faster,' he says. Beat: complicated mercy; Xanthe understands his own government is the greater monster.

chapters.title: Winter Closes Its Hand
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Snow falls without stopping—the long winter beginning early because the stars are gone. Food runs short. Tam confesses the mountain's whispers have been promising him safety if he delivers Xanthe alone. Odile nearly turns on him. Beat: fracture in the found family; trust tested by hunger and fear.

chapters.title: The Witch's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile admits she was the one who smuggled thornroot into the valley years ago—not to kill the king, but to buy passage to the Undercourt for her sister's soul, which she failed to save. She's been running this errand twice. Beat: vulnerability; Xanthe forgives her, binding the trio tighter than blood.

chapters.title: The Frozen Ferry
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. To cross the river Sere they bribe a ferryman who rows the dead. He warns them: the Undercourt honors debts, but it despises beggars—arrive owing nothing or owning everything. Xanthe gives away his last coin to a frozen child. Beat: quiet moral choice; Xanthe arrives, per the ferryman's terms, owning nothing.

chapters.title: Footprints That Walk Alone
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam disappears in the night, following the whispers. Xanthe and Odile track him to a shrine where the mountain's voice speaks through him: it offers Xanthe his mother's soul freely if he abandons his friends. Xanthe refuses aloud, and the voice screams. Beat: refusal as character; the mountain marks him.

chapters.title: The Gate Beneath the Root
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They find the entrance under a petrified tree, guarded by a door that asks each traveler what they're owed. Odile answers 'nothing'; Xanthe answers 'nothing'; the door opens. Inside, warmth like a held breath. Beat: threshold crossing; descent into wonder and menace.

chapters.title: The Court of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The Undercourt is a candlelit cavern of clerks weighing souls like coins. Xanthe finds his mother's ledger entry: sold for one winter of warmth, signed in her own hand, with a clause he wasn't meant to read—'payable in kind, or in the child.' Beat: horror and hope entangled; a loophole exists.

chapters.title: Audience with the Dying Queen
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Brought before the Queen Beneath the Mountain, Xanthe sees she is fading—the stolen stars were her attempt to hold back her own death. She offers him a bargain: his freedom for Tam, whose soul fits the ledger's weight. Beat: temptation with a friend's life as currency; the climax's stakes set.

chapters.title: Tam's Choice
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, brought below in chains, learns he was offered up. Instead of cursing Xanthe, he tells the Queen about the whispers—how she used him, how even her court's clerks pity her. His honesty cracks the courtroom's silence. Beat: the smallest member of the family becomes its bravest; the Queen wavers.

chapters.title: The Ledger Turned Backward
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Climax. Xanthe refuses all bargains and instead reads his mother's full contract aloud before the court—including the Queen's own signature swearing the debt would die with her. He argues the Undercourt's whole power rests on honoring debts; break this one and the court unmakes itself. The clerks side with him. Beat: justice won by the law beneath the law, not by force.

chapters.title: What the Queen Kept
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Queen, unbound, chooses to release the stars rather than hoard them, and dies as light returns to the sky. She gives Xanthe a single memory back—his mother's face, laughing—as her last act of grace. Odile's sister's soul walks free too. Beat: catharsis; grief finally given a face, then given peace.

chapters.title: Ascent
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The three climb out of the mountain into starlight after a long winter's night. Tam's whispers are gone; he weeps at the silence. They bury the Queen's candle above the treeline. Beat: exhaustion transformed into tenderness; the found family solidified by what they refused to trade.

chapters.title: The Kingdom That Woke Up
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Returning south, they find the wards unrenewable and the kingdom forced to govern without magic's crutch or the king's secret debts. The spymaster covers their return; the king, exposed, abdicates quietly. Xanthe is offered a place at court and declines. Beat: justice outside the law remakes the world gently.

chapters.title: Felix and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, epilogue. A year later, Xanthe runs a soup kitchen in Hollow Bells with Odile and Tam, feeding anyone who owes nothing. On the anniversary of the dark night, he tastes honey cake again—sweet, untainted—and sets a portion on the windowsill for his mother. Beat: inheritance reclaimed as nourishment; home made, not inherited.
